issues.failure_explanation: For the stated knot vector with endpoints repeated p times, a degree-p B-spline has support [t_i, t_{i+p+1}], not [t_i, t_{i+p}], and a degree-(p-1) B-spline has support [t_i, t_{i+p}], not [t_i, t_{i+p-1}]. The displayed formula is therefore off by one in the upper index for both j=1 and j=2. This propagates to the minimal-intersection interval I_k, which should have length p+1 in knot indices, and to the length check in alg:nlintersec.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the support formula to (\knot_i, \knot_{i+p+2-j}), adjust I_k to (\knot_{t_k}, \knot_{t_k+p+1}), and update the length threshold in alg:nlintersec accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of minimal intersection (def:nlintersec), the exactness criterion as applied by thm:added-1, and the support computations in alg:nlintersec and alg:shortest-chain are unreliable.
issues.title: Support formula for B-splines is off by one knot index
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and mechanical, and the overall exact-mesh framework can be preserved after consistently shifting the support length; no global proof architecture is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Next, let \(\mathcal{R}^{\boldvec{j}'}_{\meshel, \tilde{\level}}\) be the smallest subset of \(\bspbasis^{\boldvec{j}'}_{\tilde{\level}}\) that can be linearly combined to represent \(\bsp^{\boldvec{j}'}_{\boldvec{i}', \level}\) on \(\meshel\).

issues.failure_explanation: The truncation operator keeps only B-splines whose support is not contained in the refinement domain. Vanishing of the truncated function on Q means the kept B-splines sum to zero on Q; it does not mean the mother B-spline's representation on Q is supported inside the domain. The proof's central inference is therefore false.

failure_location.quote: Since \(\thb^{\boldvec{j}}_{\boldvec{i}, \level}\) vanishes on \(\meshel\), we know that the support of B-splines in \(\mathcal{R}^{\boldvec{j}}_{Q, \tilde{\level}}\) is contained in \(\Omega_{\tilde{\level}}\).

issues.title: Proof of support containment for truncated B-splines confuses truncated function with its mother

issues.failure_explanation: If i_k = j_k, no neighbor in direction k is closer to j_k, so the lemma's first inference is false. A problematic pair can have i_k = j_k for a resolved direction, making the lemma false as stated.

failure_location.quote: Since \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{i}}\) is resolved in direction \(k\), by definition there exists \(\xbsp_{\boldvec{t}}\in \sideconfig_{\boldvec{i},k}\) such that \(\abs{t_k - j_k} < \abs{i_k - j_k|\).
